data.description:
## Observed

Gerrit change 3191 (story 7a7a-ceb9-e9a5-4d8e) took `Verified -1` after a local
`make verify` returned rc=0 (20,135 passed). All 4 CI pytest cells failed
deterministically on the same test:

    tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py
      ::test_no_test_addresses_a_bare_repository_by_discovery

Failing cells: ubuntu py3.11, py3.12, py3.13, macos py3.13
(run 41271076673). The failure was a true positive — a real policy violation
in the changed tree, not a flake.

## Root cause of the MISS (not of the test failure)

`make test` selects `-m "not integration and not external"`. That selection
deselects the entire policy module:

    $ pytest tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py \
        -q -m "not integration and not external" --collect-only
    no tests collected (6 deselected) in 0.31s

So `make verify` CANNOT fail on this module, while CI's gating
`ubuntu-latest, py3.13` cell DOES run it and DID fail on it.

## Why this matters

`AGENTS.md` states that `make test` "selects exactly what CI's gating
`ubuntu-latest, py3.13` cell selects (`not integration and not external`) — a
superset of every other matrix cell — so it is the locally checkable half of
`Verified`, with nothing to enumerate and nothing to drift."

The CI evidence above contradicts the parenthetical: the gating cell's
selection is NOT `not integration and not external`, because it ran an
integration-tier test. Either the documented contract or the `make test`
selection is wrong. Today an author who follows the documented contract
exactly can still be pushed red — which is the same class as bug
1035-bed7-c855-4732, recurring through a different hole.

This is a contract/trust defect, not a test defect: the value of `make verify`
is that "I verified this" is a true statement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The actual marker selection used by CI's gating `ubuntu-latest, py3.13`
      cell is read from `.github/workflows/` and recorded verbatim on this
      ticket.
- [ ] `make test`'s selection and the gating cell's selection are shown to
      agree, either by changing `make test` to match CI or by changing the CI
      cell to match `make test` — whichever preserves the documented intent
      that local verify is the locally checkable half of `Verified`.
- [ ] A test asserts the two selections agree, so they cannot silently drift
      again (the repo already has CI-workflow parity tests; extend one rather
      than adding a new mechanism).
- [ ] `AGENTS.md`'s claim is corrected to match whatever the resolved contract
      is, including the "superset of every other matrix cell" clause.
- [ ] Demonstrated: with the fix in place, a tree containing the 7a7a
      violation fails `make verify` locally.
data.title: make test excludes the integration tier that CI's gating cell runs
